title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp. 54-57). Grothendieck is building an axiomatic, combinatorial 'analysis situs', in the spirit of the tame topology programme of the Esquisse. There is a structure M = (M, ≤, ≪) of elementary 'pieces' (model example on p. 57: simplices in a topological space, ≤ = face relation). There are 'figures' F built from pieces, each with a poset F̃ of sub-figures. The 'ombre' omb(X) is the set of points (elements of a dense part Λ) lying in X. The canonical map φ_Λ : F → Fig(Λ), F ↦ mul omb_Λ(F), sends a figure to its multi-shadow in Λ. Λ is a dense sub-structure, an 'atlas'.

Lemma 1 (p. 55): φ_Λ is strict, i.e. for every F, F' ↦ φ_Λ(F') gives an isomorphism of ordered sets F̃ ≅ (φ_Λ(F))~.

On this page:
(1) The lemma was already seen for Λ = M. The general case reduces to it via the inclusion i : Λ → M and the associated figure Φ ∈ Fig(M). The key input is density: for every X ∈ Φ the interior X° meets Λ, i.e. i*(X°) ≠ ∅. Applying this with Λ = L gives statement a), strictness.
(2) Proof of c). Claim: if φ(F) and φ(G) are in 'good relative position' (their shadows meet along a common sub-figure; the relation written with a crossed symbol, cf. ⋔-negated on p. 55), then so are F and G. Using a), the largest common sub-figure of φ(F) and φ(G) should be φ(L), where L = F ∩ G := Inf(F,G), so that L̃ = F̃ ∩ G̃.
  - φ(L) is certainly a common sub-figure. If Φ is the largest one, then φ(L) ⊂ Φ.
  - By strictness, Φ = φ(L') = φ(L'') with L' ≤ F, L'' ≤ G and L ≤ L', L''.
  - One wants L' = L'', hence L' = L'' = L. Grothendieck stresses that φ need not be injective.
  - If L' ≠ L'', pick X ∈ L̃' \ L̃. By a) there is a unique Y ∈ L̃'' \ L̃ with φ(X) = φ(Y).
  - Then the largest common sub-figure of X and Y is X ∩ L = Y ∩ L, distinct from X and Y. Here φ(X), φ(Y) are trivially in good position (they are equal) while X, Y are not.
  - He asks 'Est-ce bien impossible?'.
(3) The next page answers no. Put two different affine structures on an arc in a space. This gives two 1-simplices X ≠ Y with the same boundary and the same shadow, so φ(X) = φ(Y) but X and Y are not compatible.
(4) Conclusion (Cor., p. 57): (i) ⇒ (ii) + injectivity of φ, and (ii) + injectivity of φ ⇒ (i).

So the page is a routine verification step in an axiomatic framework. It locates exactly where injectivity of the shadow map is needed.
errors: The attempted proof of c) cannot be completed without extra hypotheses: the argument stalls at L' = L'', and Grothendieck himself flags this ('φ peut ne pas l'être', 'Est-ce bien impossible?'). Page 57 confirms the gap with a counterexample and repairs it by adding injectivity of φ. This is self-correction, not a hidden error.
Minor: the reduction of the general Λ to Λ = M is only sketched (density gives i*(X°) ≠ ∅); details are left implicit.

ideas.what: Shadow / multi-shadow map from abstract figures to sets of points of a dense sub-atlas; strictness (bijection on sub-figure posets)
ideas.modern_name: Comparison of a combinatorial (simplicial/stratified) structure with its geometric realization; faithfulness of realization on face posets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical combinatorial topology; in tame-topology form, o-minimal cell decomposition (van den Dries, Knight-Pillay-Steinhorn, 1980s-90s)
ideas.where_published: Programmatic only: Esquisse d'un programme §5 (topologie modérée); this axiomatics unpublished

ideas.what: Density of Λ in M used as 'interior of each piece meets Λ' to reduce the general strictness lemma to Λ = M

Observation that good relative position of shadows need not lift to the figures, because the shadow map can be non-injective (two affine structures on one arc); injectivity of φ is the missing condition
ideas.modern_name: Non-uniqueness of PL/affine structure on a given underlying set; realization does not determine the simplicial structure

missed.claim: Part of Grothendieck's unpublished 1986 axiomatization of 'analysis situs' (tame topology) via posets of figures with relations ≤, ≪ and compatibility, plus a shadow functor to point sets. This page only fixes a lemma and isolates injectivity of φ as the needed hypothesis. The framework as a whole was never developed by others in this form.
missed.quote: NB on ne sait pas si φ est injectif, et φ peut ne pas l'être...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Modest. It documents how Grothendieck intended to axiomatize tame topology combinatorially, an alternative to o-minimality. The specific lemma is routine.

deep.surprise_reason: A technical verification inside an unpublished axiomatic framework, with a standard counterexample appearing on the next page. It is of historical interest as evidence of the 1986 'analysis situs' programme, but contains no new theorem or connection.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: likely 'c'est un truc/exercice..., se ramène par applic. aux quelc[onques] i : Λ → M et figures assoc. Φ ∈ Fig(M), grâce à [?] ∀X ∈ Φ, i*(X°) ≠ ∅'. The phrase is 'se ramène par application', not 'pour notre cas'.
'Supposons φ(F) ≤ φ(G)' and 'φ(X) ≤ φ(Y)', 'X ≤ Y': the symbol in the image is a crossed relation (≭-like, the compatibility / non-transversality relation used with ⋔ on p. 55), not ≤.
'soit X^p ∈ ..., L̃'\L̃' should read 'soit X ∈ L̃' \ L̃'.
'une unique Y ∈ L̃''\L̃ telle que φ(X) = φ(Y)'. In the image X and Y are partly overwritten/crossed in places, but this is the intended reading.
'(s'— pour ceci)' in the margin perhaps '(sera prouvé ceci)' or similar; illegible.
